INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which feature of indifference curve theory is most likely to apply in reality?

options.A: The consumer can express preferences between all possible combinations of goods.
options.B: The consumer has a limited income to spend.
options.C: The consumer will always behave rationally.
options.D: The consumer will always get positive utility from having more of the goods.

options.A: falling returns to scale average cost is greater than marginal cost
options.B: falling returns to scale rising returns to scale

options.D: unit cost falls as output increases unit cost rises as output increases

questions.questionText: A government makes it compulsory for motorbike riders to wear helmets. What would represent a positive externality of consumption associated with this decision?

options.A: decreased pressure on the provision of health care
options.B: expenses incurred on surveillance of motorbike riders to ensure compliance
options.C: increased life expectancy of motorbike riders

questions.questionText: The table shows the market shares of firms selling a very similar product in a country between 2018 and 2020. firm 2018 2020 Norton 28.4 27.4 Souton 18.9 17.6 Eastern 17.1 14.7 Western 12.5 11.4 Scotsdale 7.2 8.5 Welshpool 5.8 8.2 Greenland 3.9 4.8 Franklin 2.2 3.6 Bellweather 2.1 1.9 others 1.9 1.9 What can be concluded from the data between the two years?

options.B: Sales of the top four firms fell.
options.D: The concentration ratio of the four largest firms fell.

A bus company has a monopoly and specialises in long-distance travel. It initially sells its tickets to customers one month in advance of the journey. As the departure date approaches, the price of a ticket increases. Which kind of pricing policy does the bus company operate?

The diagram shows the marginal private benefit (MPB), the marginal private cost (MPC) and the marginal social cost (MSC) for firms in an industry. The equilibrium price is point X. price MSC MPC X MPB = MSB O quantity What should happen to achieve allocative efficiency?

options.A: a decrease in consumption and an increase in price
options.B: a decrease in production and no change in price
options.C: an increase in consumption and a decrease in production
options.D: an increase in price and no change in production

questions.questionText: Firm X is considering whether to co-operate with its rival so that their joint profit is $4000 a month ($2000 each). It calculated that, if it did not co-operate, its own profit would be $2800 a month provided it kept all its customers itself. However, if its rival undercut X’s price and took some of X’s customers then X’s profit would be $1200. It has no knowledge of what the rival’s policy will be. What describes the situation that the firm is facing?
A smartphone manufacturing company takes over an electronic chip design company. This is an example of which type of growth?
What is not a valid comment economists may make regarding the need to subsidise a green energy market that uses solar and wind power?

options.A: It is cheaper to use the plentiful supply of coal.
options.C: The value of the positive externalities cannot be estimated.
options.D: The value of the negative externalities cannot be estimated.

questions.questionText: In which situation is the introduction of a minimum wage most likely to raise employment opportunities as well as wages?

options.A: Firms face intense competition both at home and abroad.
options.B: Labour costs are a high proportion of the total cost of the firm.
options.C: The minimum wage is not high enough to lower the profits of the firms.
options.D: The minimum wage introduced in monopsony is less than the marginal revenue productivity (MRP) of the last worker employed.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s initial marginal revenue product of labour curve (MRP ). marginal revenue product of labour MRP MRP O labour hours What could cause the curve to shift to MRP ?

options.A: a fall in the wage rate
options.B: a fall in the price of the final product
options.C: a rise in the wage rate
options.D: a rise in the price of the final product

questions.questionText: A firm operates in a perfectly competitive labour market. The table shows the marginal revenue product (MRP) and marginal cost of labour (MCL) for each additional worker employed by this profit-maximising firm. units of labour MRP MCL employed
Countries in South East Asia have some of the highest income inequality in the world. Which policy could be adopted by governments in South East Asia to reduce income inequality in the short run?

options.A: Increase the general sales tax/VAT rate on luxury goods.
options.C: Invest heavily in schools and education programmes.
options.D: Stimulate economic growth through skills and productivity training.

questions.questionText: When buying a car, Salma agrees to pay half of the cost now and the other half in six months time. Which function of money does this illustrate?
When is the natural rate of unemployment most likely to fall?

options.A: when there is a decline in the education levels of workers
options.B: when there is an increase in income tax rates
options.C: when there is an increase in labour mobility
options.D: when there is a rise in the rate of state unemployment benefits

Which argument for lowering income tax rates is always valid?

options.B: It promotes the incentive to work.
options.D: It reduces the incentive to evade taxes.
